scope: C++ inference engine CUDA matmul dispatch (independent acceleration track)

design.bridge: src/cuda_bridge.cpp — host-API-only cuBLAS Dgemm (fp64) with per-call H2D/D2H; compiled as plain C++ (no nvcc/device kernels — CUDA 12.0 cudafe++ incompatible with MSVC 18; kernels need compatible toolchain or precompiled cubin later)
design.dispatch: matmul() routes to GPU only when XINGCHENG_CPP_CUDA=1 read at engine load; env unset -> C-core CPU path unchanged; env set without CUDA build/device -> CUDA_UNAVAILABLE fail-closed at load
design.governance: capability in native layer; enablement decided by governed Python env — consistent with 'native provides execution, Python owns policy'; gpu_coordinator semantics apply to the Python caller
design.build: build_cpp.py detects CUDA_PATH/cublas and links cudart+cublas; cpp_runtime.load_extension registers CUDA bin via os.add_dll_directory (Win32 ignores PATH for pyd deps)
design.layering: native/ pure-C core untouched — acceleration lives in the C++ layer per blueprint 'GPU 為獨立加速軌'

validation.build: extension builds with XINGCHENG_CUDA=1, links cudart64_12+cublas64_12 (CUDA 12.0)
validation.tests: 29 passed in 17.07s (3 new: opt-in logits parity atol 1e-6, opt-in greedy generation parity vs CPU, default-CPU unchanged; all skip cleanly without a device)
validation.device: real RTX GPU present; torch.cuda.is_available()=True; tests exercised the GPU path
validation.fail_closed: CUDA_UNAVAILABLE when requested without build/device; CUDA_MATMUL_FAILED on bridge errors

remaining: device-resident weights (v1 copies per call), bf16/fp32 GEMM paths, GPU-resident KV cache, production routing through gpu_coordinator, long-duration validation (P3f)
